added.name: 'should clear the active item in key manager when the last focused chip is destroyed'

decision: The complete two-file14-hunk chip test change activates one previously commented destruction registration, not an xit. It creates InputChipGrid, patches focus, empties a signal and checks activeItemIndex after stability. Of119 retained static cases112 callback semantics are unchanged and seven changes are individually accounted for: one array observer becomes a signal read; six listbox callbacks extract eight identical-duration timer operations, including one added fixture.whenStable before inspecting initial async chips. InputChipGrid changes its eight-value mutable array, add/remove identity and @for binding into a readonly signal with fresh-array updates; these notifications and rendering are not declared equivalent. Adapt only the destruction purpose to the owned legacy MatChipList. A demonstrated stale reference is repaired by updateActiveItem(-1) for an empty QueryList, preserving neighbor/refocus behavior; append one lifecycle regression covering destruction, repopulation and fresh focus while preserving all2222 old cases and all production HTML/CSS/SCSS. The isolated actual-method controls use public QueryList/FocusKeyManager with fake chips, not a full Angular component or21.x floor. Its source context83/native bindings20/generic records13/import receipts27 has been qualified and original programs retained through immutable replay. Decline the modern grid/signal fixture migration. The new real Angular case and packed/browser/both-floor execution remain mandatory and unexecuted.
